methodology.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
methodology.value: Online survey with a vignette experiment administered via the I&O Research entrepreneurs' panel to 445 owners/managers of Dutch small- and medium-sized enterprises (EU Recommendation 2003/361/EC SME definition). Respondents rated inclination to pay under systematically varied scenario factors (ransom affordability, existence of backups, advice from a cybersecurity company). Data analysed in R with regression models, consistent with a rational-choice / situational-crime-prevention framing. Record verified against Crossref DOI metadata (58 references) and the SAGE article abstract.

methodology.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
methodology.value: Quantitative analysis of 502 ransomware attacks reported to the Dutch national police between 2019 and 2022, of which 104 (20.7%) targeted Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices such as QNAP units, spanning both households and organisations. Victim characteristics, attack characteristics and financial impact of NAS versus non-NAS attacks are compared, framed with routine activity theory and the CRAVED/target-suitability literature. The paper additionally reconstructs the October 2022 Dutch police intervention against a QNAP-NAS ransomware strain (DeadBolt), in which the police used a bitcoin payment trick to obtain decryption keys and offer free victim decryption. Record verified against Crossref DOI metadata (60 references), the Taylor & Francis journal page and the University of Twente Pure open-access record.

key_findings.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
key_findings.value: The stated likelihood of paying the ransom is low among Dutch SME decision-makers. Being advised to pay by a cybersecurity company significantly increases the likelihood of paying, as does not having a backup. Unexpectedly, the affordability of the ransom demand is not significantly related to the payment decision. Implications: backup adoption and professional-advice norms (rather than ransom size) are the key levers for reducing payment vulnerability and extortion profitability.

key_findings.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
key_findings.value: NAS devices account for a substantial minority of reported attacks: 104 of 502 police-reported ransomware attacks (20.7%) targeted NAS devices, affecting both individuals and companies. Financial impact of an attack on an individual NAS owner is relatively low compared with organisational attacks, but the emotional loss of personal photos/videos makes NAS victimization painful and under-addressed in the public ransomware debate. The October 2022 police intervention against the QNAP-NAS strain demonstrated that law enforcement can convert tracing/seizure into free victim decryption.

limitations.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
limitations.value: Stated payment intentions in hypothetical vignettes may not equal real payment behaviour (social desirability/hypothetical bias); single-country (Dutch) sample limits external validity; survey sampling via a commercial panel may skew towards more cyber-aware entrepreneurs; inability vs willingness to pay not fully disentangled. Authors acknowledge that actual victimization conditions may differ from the manipulated vignette factors.

limitations.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
limitations.value: Data derive from police reports with possible low willingness to report (both individuals and SMEs under-report), so the 20.7% NAS share may not generalise to the true attack population; single-country (Netherlands) register; attack reports include incomplete or victim-supplied details; the law-enforcement intervention case study is a single episode. Authors explicitly name low reporting willingness as the main sample limitation.

research_gaps.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
research_gaps.value: Addresses the gap that little is known about how SMEs respond to ransomware victimization and which factors drive the payment decision - prior ransomware victim studies concentrated on prevalence and large enterprises. Leaves open real-payment validation, cross-jurisdiction replication, and study of negotiator/insurer influence.

research_gaps.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
research_gaps.value: Addresses the gap that ransomware research overwhelmingly focuses on Windows endpoints and enterprise double-extortion campaigns, largely ignoring consumer/SOHO NAS appliances as a distinct victim population. Highlights that NAS ransomware needs inclusion in the public debate and in victimology/cyberinsurance research; open questions include true prevalence beyond police reports and effectiveness of interventions.

dataset_benchmark.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
dataset_benchmark.value: Primary survey data: N = 445 Dutch SME owners/managers recruited through the I&O Research entrepreneurs' panel, with embedded factorial vignette design; no named public security benchmark; open data sharing not stated in the indexed record ([uncertain] whether the dataset is open-sourced)

dataset_benchmark.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
dataset_benchmark.value: Dutch police ransomware-attack register extract: 502 reported attacks (2019-2022), 104 NAS-targeted; supplemented by Censys internet-exposure tracking evidence referenced for DeadBolt; no open-sourced dataset identified in the indexed record ([uncertain] whether the dataset is open-sourced)

evaluation_metrics.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
evaluation_metrics.value: Statistical effect metrics rather than security metrics: logistic/OLS regression coefficients and odds ratios for payment-decision factors (advice to pay, backup availability, ransom affordability), predicted payment likelihood; no F1/precision/recall or detection-latency metrics (survey-based social-science design)

evaluation_metrics.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
evaluation_metrics.value: Descriptive and comparative victimology metrics: proportion of NAS-targeted attacks (20.7% of 502), victim type split (individuals vs organisations), financial impact (ransom requested, ransom paid, financial loss) of NAS vs non-NAS attacks; no detection/ML metrics (criminological register study)

reproducibility.paper: Examining ransomware payment decision-making among small- and medium-sized enterprises
reproducibility.value: Moderate: vignette design, panel recruitment and R-based analysis are described in the paper (analysis in R/stattricks tooling per reference list), supporting methodological replication; but individual survey micro-data are held by the research team and public release is not confirmed, limiting full reproduction ([uncertain] data availability)

reproducibility.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
reproducibility.value: Low-to-moderate: analysis of a privileged police dataset that cannot be redistributed; strings/coding scheme and the October 2022 DeadBolt intervention (Chainalysis/Censys/BleepingComputer evidence) are traceable via open sources, but external researchers cannot re-run the exact register analysis; no external validation environment

threat_actor_fields.value: Not applicable: no RaaS group named, no leak-site evidence, no payment wallet/tracing coverage; the paper studies victim-side decisions rather than actor attribution

threat_actor_fields.paper: NAS ransomware: ransomware targeting NAS devices
threat_actor_fields.value: Partial coverage: names consumer-NAS ransomware strains/campaigns (DeadBolt, ech0raix, Qlocker targeting QNAP devices) rather than RaaS groups; documents the October 2022 law-enforcement action where the Dutch police tricked the DeadBolt actor into releasing decryption keys (bitcoin-trick key recovery supported by Chainalysis evidence); no leak-site or RaaS-affiliate attribution analysis
